items.followUp: State Newton's second law in terms of momentum and write its equation.

rubric.why: Checks the verbal relation between force and momentum.
rubric.description: States that force is the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating this relation.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical expression of the relation.
rubric.description: Writes force as the change in momentum per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation.

rubric.why: Checks the expression for momentum used in deriving the relation.
rubric.description: States that momentum is mass multiplied by velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct momentum expression.

rubric.why: Checks the relation for constant mass.
rubric.description: Shows that the force relation becomes F = ma for constant mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct resulting relation.

modelAnswer: According to Newton's second law, the force acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of its momentum.
Since momentum p = mv, for mass m changing velocity from u to v in time t:
F = change in momentum / time = (mv − mu) / t.
For constant mass, F = m(v − u) / t = ma.

items.followUp: What is the prefix kilo? Give its symbol and value.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of prefixes and what they indicate.
rubric.description: Defines prefixes as words or symbols placed before units to indicate multiples or submultiples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that prefixes go before units and indicate multiples or submultiples.

rubric.why: Checks the practical usefulness of prefixes.
rubric.description: Explains that prefixes make very large or very small measurements convenient to express.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are words or symbols placed before units to indicate multiples or submultiples of the units.
They are useful because they make very large or very small measurements convenient to express.
